mentions.name: Got
mentions.description: This is a version control system like Git, designed to handle files and directories of any size, with end-to-end encryption. It is built on top of Blobcache, a transactional storage layer.

mentions.name: Got Version Control
mentions.description: Git-like version control system that fixes the problems of storing large files and directories in Git: no separate large-files provider to configure and all commit data goes to the same place. It stores file data in Blobcache and encrypts everything end-to-end, making it suitable for versioning an entire home directory. GPL-licensed FOSS with contributions welcome.
mentions.problem: Storing large files and directories in Git is problematic and requires separately configured large-file providers, making it hard to put a whole home directory under version control.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm also working on Got Version Control https://github.com/gotvc/got

Got uses Blobcache for storing file data.

Got is like Git, if you fixed all the problems with storing large files and directories in Git.
There's no "large files provider" to configure separately.
All the data for a commit goes to the same place.
Got also encrypts all the data you put in it, E2E.
If you've run into problems putting your whole home directory in Git, you might have more luck with Got.
